UK Tourist Visa for Indians in 2026 - here's what the process actually looks like.

The UK Standard Visitor Visa lets Indian tourists visit England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland for up to 6 months. It's thorough but straightforward if your documents are clean.

📋 WHAT YOU NEED:

✅ Valid passport (6 months+ beyond your travel date)
✅ Completed UK Visa application form (online via gov.uk)
✅ Biometrics appointment at VFS UK centre in Mumbai
✅ Confirmed return flight tickets
✅ Hotel bookings for the full duration
✅ Bank statements — last 3–6 months (consistent balance, not a last-minute top-up)
✅ Salary slips / ITR for the last 2 years
✅ Leave letter from employer on company letterhead
✅ Travel itinerary and cover letter

💷 FEES (2026):
Standard 6-month visa: £115 (~₹12,200)
2-year multiple entry: £400 (~₹42,500)
5-year multiple entry: £750 (~₹79,500)
VFS service fee: ~₹2,500 (non-refundable)

⏱️ PROCESSING TIME:
Standard: 3 weeks from biometrics
Priority (additional fee): 5 business days
Super Priority: Next working day (very limited slots)

⚠️ 2026 UPDATE:
English language requirements were raised for student and work visas in 2025 — tourist visas are NOT affected. Application process for tourists remains unchanged.

We handle UK visa documentation, VFS appointment booking, and application review from our Malad West office.

Singapore in 5 days - the plan that actually works.

Singapore is one of the cleanest, safest, most organised travel destinations in Asia. It also rewards a tight, well-planned itinerary more than almost anywhere else.

📍 Day 1: Marina Bay
Marina Bay Sands SkyPark, Gardens by the Bay (Supertrees at night are extraordinary), Merlion Park. The city skyline from the waterfront at 8 PM is one of the best urban views in the world.

📍 Day 2: Sentosa Island
Universal Studios Singapore (2–3 hours minimum), Adventure Cove Waterpark, S.E.A. Aquarium, cable car ride across the bay.

📍 Day 3: Culture & Heritage
Chinatown — Sri Mariamman Temple, Maxwell Food Centre for the most famous chicken rice in Singapore. Little India — Mustafa Centre (open 24 hours). Arab Street — Sultan Mosque, textiles.

📍 Day 4: Zoo & Night Safari
Singapore Zoo is consistently rated among the world's best. The Night Safari — the world's first nocturnal wildlife park — opens at 7:30 PM. Do both if you have energy.

📍 Day 5: Orchard Road & depart
Shopping, hawker centres, Jewel Changi Airport before your flight (the indoor waterfall alone is worth the visit).

🛂 Singapore Visa for Indians
India and Singapore now have a reciprocal 30-day visa-free arrangement as of 2024. Check your passport validity — 6 months minimum required.

💰 Trip cost from Mumbai: ₹90,000–₹1,40,000 per person (7 nights, mid-range)

🌧️ Everyone waits for December. Smart travellers book July–September.

Here's what monsoon actually gives you in three of India's best destinations:

🌊 GOA
The crowds are gone. Resorts drop prices 25–40%. The landscape turns dramatically green. The Fort Aguada cliffs, the Fontainhas Latin Quarter, the spice plantations — all of it without a tourist bus in sight. Beach swimming is restricted, but the culture and food experience is better than peak season.

🌿 KERALA
Ayurvedic practitioners say monsoon is when treatments work best. The backwaters in Alleppey are fuller. The Munnar tea estates are greener than you've ever seen them. Houseboat prices are negotiable. This is the quiet, lush version of Kerala most people never experience.

 COORG
Coorg in July–August is completely different from the dry-season version. Rain-soaked coffee estates, waterfalls running at full force, mist over the Brahmagiri hills. Stays at coffee estate bungalows are both cheaper and more atmospheric.

Our domestic packages cover all three - with flexible dates built around your schedule.

October is the single best month to visit Rajasthan. Here's why you should book now.

All year, people ask, "When should we go to Rajasthan?" The answer is always October–February. And October specifically gives you something special:

→ Pushkar Camel Fair falls in November (book NOW if you want accommodation)

Nepal: no passport needed, no visa fees, and mountains that will stop you mid-sentence.

For Indian travelers, Nepal is the easiest international trip possible. Your Aadhaar card gets you in. And what you get in return is one of the most dramatic landscapes on earth.

Our 5-night itinerary:

📍 Day 1–2: Kathmandu
Pashupatinath Temple — one of the most sacred Shiva temples in the world, on the banks of the Bagmati river. Boudhanath Stupa — the largest Buddhist stupa in Asia. Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple). Durbar Square.
Evening: Thamel market for local shopping and momos.

📍 Day 3: Drive to Pokhara
The 6-hour drive through the hills is scenic enough to count as a sightseeing activity. Or fly (30 mins, worth every rupee).

📍 Day 4: Pokhara
🌅 Sarangkot sunrise — the most famous view in Nepal. Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, and Machhapuchchhre (Fishtail Mountain) lit up in gold at dawn.
Phewa Lake boat ride. World Peace Pagoda. Davis Falls (underground waterfall).

📍 Day 5: Pokhara adventure day
Paragliding over Pokhara — 30 minutes in the air with the Himalayas on all sides. The video alone is worth it.
Begnas Lake, Gupteshwor Cave.

📍 Day 6: Return to Kathmandu & depart

✅ No visa, no passport needed for Indians
✈️ IndiGo, Air India, and Buddha Air operate frequent routes

Oman: the most underrated destination in the Middle East. And arguably the most beautiful.

While everyone's talking about Dubai, Oman quietly offers something Dubai can't — ancient forts, untouched wadis, dramatic desert, and a coastline with zero crowds.

Our 7-day Oman itinerary:

📍 Day 1–2: Muscat
Mutrah Souq (the most authentic Arab bazaar you'll find), Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque (one of the most stunning mosques in the world), Royal Opera House, Corniche waterfront.

📍 Day 3: Nizwa & Jabrin Fort
Oman's ancient capital. Nizwa Fort dates back to the 17th century. Jabrin Castle has some of the most intricate painted wooden ceilings in the region.

📍 Day 4: Wadi Shab & Wadi Bani Khalid
Wadi Shab is Oman's most famous canyon — turquoise pools, natural caves, and a swim through emerald water to reach a hidden waterfall.

📍 Day 5–6: Wahiba Sands (Desert Camp)
Overnight in a Bedouin-style desert camp. Dune bashing, camel ride at sunset, stargazing with no light pollution. Mornings in the Wahiba are silent and extraordinary.

📍 Day 7: Sur & Ras Al Jinz
Watch Olive Ridley sea turtles nest and hatch (seasonal) at Ras Al Jinz Turtle Reserve. Sur dhow-building yards — centuries-old tradition still alive.

✅ India-Oman e-Visa: processed online, valid for 30 days
✈️ Direct flights from Mumbai, Kochi, Hyderabad

Mauritius: where the Indian Ocean does its best work. 5 days of pure beach luxury.

Mauritius isn't just a holiday. It's the kind of trip that makes you forget what day of the week it is.

Our 5-day package covers everything:

🏖️ Day 1–2: Beachfront Resort
Arrive and check into your beachside property. Lagoon swimming, sunset cocktails, and that first moment when you realise your phone can wait.

⛵ Day 3: Catamaran Cruise
Full-day catamaran trip along the coast — snorkelling in crystal-clear water, dolphin spotting (morning hours), and a BBQ lunch on board. This is the highlight for most travellers.

🌈 Day 4: Chamarel & the South
Chamarel's Seven Coloured Earths — volcanic soil in seven distinct colours, no two patches alike. Chamarel Rum Distillery. Rochester Falls. Black River Gorges National Park.

🛍️ Day 5: Port Louis
The capital's Central Market (spices, local crafts), the waterfront Caudan district, and a final beach evening before departure.

✅ Visa-free for Indian passport holders (30-day entry)
✈️ Direct flights from Mumbai, Delhi & Chennai

Mauritius is one of the few places where budget and luxury feel equally at home. Our packages cover both, let us know which fits you.

Andaman Islands: one of India's best beach destinations. Here's when to go and what to expect.

The Andamans are genuinely in a different league - white sand, turquoise water, some of Asia's best coral reefs, and far fewer crowds than Goa.

🗓️ WHEN TO GO:

🏆 October–March (Peak Season)
→ Best weather, calm sea, perfect for water sports
→ Scuba diving, snorkelling, sea walking — all available
→ Ideal for couples and honeymoon trips
→ Book early — good resorts fill up fast

💸 June–September (Monsoon = Budget Season)
→ Seas are rough, most water sports suspended
→ Ferries run on reduced schedules
→ BUT: prices drop significantly on hotels and packages
→ Lush green landscapes, peaceful beaches

🏄 Activities by season:
→ Scuba diving & sea walk: October to May only (water clarity)
→ Romantic beach evenings: November to April
→ Budget travel: June to September

📦 What our Andaman packages include:
✅ Flights from Mumbai (direct)
✅ Airport-to-hotel transfers
✅ Hotel stays
✅ Port Blair → Havelock island ferry
✅ Guided tours — Cellular Jail, Ross Island, Radhanagar Beach

🌟 Fun fact: Andaman is one of the most affordable beach holiday destinations in India - cheaper than Goa resorts in peak season for comparable quality.

Kashi, Gaya, and Prayagraj are three of Hinduism's most sacred cities. One unforgettable 4-night pilgrimage.

This is the journey that matters most in a Hindu devotee's lifetime. We make it comfortable, meaningful, and completely arranged.

📍 Prayagraj (Day 1)
Triveni Sangam — the confluence of Ganga, Yamuna, and the invisible Saraswati. Take a holy dip. Visit Anand Bhavan (Nehru family home, now a museum). Allahabad Fort.

📍 Varanasi / Kashi (Days 2-3) 🌟
The oldest living city on earth.
→ Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat at sunset - one of the most powerful spiritual experiences in India
→ Pre-dawn boat ride on the Ganga — watch the city wake up from the river
→ Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga (one of the 12 Jyotirlingas)
→ Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple
→ Sarnath - where the Buddha gave his first sermon, just 10 km from Varanasi

📍 Gaya & Bodh Gaya (Day 4)
Vishnupad Temple - where Lord Vishnu's footprint is enshrined
Bodh Gaya - the spot under the Bodhi tree where the Buddha attained enlightenment (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
Mahabodhi Temple - one of the most sacred Buddhist pilgrimage sites in the world

The package includes trains/flights, hotel, all transfers, meals, and a local guide at each destination
